html:
Welcome to the official RaggieSoft Backstage companion archive for Katie & Nathaniel.

Because every chapter of Katie & Nathaniel is written strictly in Nathaniel Prairie's first-person point of view, the main novel only shows what Nate and Katie can directly see, hear, and deduce in the moment. Whenever you encounter a Backstage Bonus Feature button at the end of a chapter on , you can open these behind-the-scenes dossiers directly inside the reader without breaking narrative immersion.

Complete Chronological Index of Behind-the-Scenes Dossiers (2001–2044)

  1. Oct 19, 2001 — The Sunward Tropics Security File & How Brenda Lost the 'Prairie' Surname
    What happened behind closed doors when Brenda's attorney walked into Arthur Vance's conference room off Independence Boulevard to watch the M/S Sunward Tropics Deck 4 security tape—and how Katie and Nate's request forced Brenda to sign the Va. Code § 20-121.4 stipulation surrendering the Prairie family name and reverting to Brenda Walsh.
  2. Dec 27, 2004 — Dirty Old Tonomy Hill & The Williamsburg Transportation Center 'What If'
    Why developmentally disabled Cousin Chelsea actually held the sole legal authority on the Newport Housing Authority lease to evict Tiffany Sloan from her apartment on Tonomy Hill at any time—and the canonical "What If" exploring what would have happened on Monday, December 27, 2004 if nineteen-year-old Nate had rolled off the southbound Pathfinder coach during its fifteen-minute layover two blocks from Katie's apartment in Williamsburg.
  3. Nov 13–15, 2005 — CBSA Secondary Inspection at 35 Park Street East & The U.S. Marshals File on Brandon Mercer
    Reconstructs the twenty-eight hours between Katie's 4:01 PM escape on the CTTA Grey Line bus in Williamsburg and Brandon Mercer's arrest by Deputy U.S. Marshals at a men's shelter on Cass Avenue in Detroit—including his refusal of entry into Canada at 555 Goyeau Street and 35 Park Street East in Windsor, Ontario and the CBP seizure of his two external hard drives at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street.
  4. Mar 8–15, 2007 — The Unopened RRC Staff Dossier: Form A vs. Form B & The Unsigned Level 1 Contract
    Opens the internal Bates-Harding staff notes on "Prairie, Nathaniel" and "Prairie, Katherine"—revealing why Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller separated their tests into Form A and Form B expecting them to cheat on the outdated 1996 exam battery, why VITA locked down the lab on Quantum OS 2000 Professional, and the drafted Level 1 Restriction & Mandatory Separation Contract sitting on their counselor's desk on Thursday morning.
  5. Mar 13, 2007 — The 11:00 PM Curfew Search & Why Locking the Seasonal Closet Door Got Nate and Katie Caught
    Discover how Barton Hall dorm staff tracked Nate and Katie to the Rec Hall without an on-campus sign-out sheet—and why locking a normally unlocked door in a notorious student hookup closet is the exact thing that tipped the night supervisor off while the twins were hidden in the dark.
  6. Mar 14–15, 2007 — How Christopher Vance Scrambled the Dorm Roster & The Thursday Morning Cover-Up
    What happened behind closed doors when Christopher Vance stole an open administrative login to swap opposite-gender dorm room assignments on Wednesday night, why RRC whisked him onto a bus in Staunton at 7:50 AM on Thursday without calling the State Police, and why Nate and Katie's 10:00 AM Level 1 disciplinary counselor meeting never happened.
  7. Oct 28, 2010 — The 509 East 18th Street Executive Suite, Mayor Overton's Bus, & Harold Dietz's 0.4% Collapse
    Why CVTA CEO Leonard Sterling and COO Richard Halstead blackballed Nate from TRAC, the real Tidewater municipal history of the Newtown Road bus-border cliff that haunted Mayor Myra E. Overton, why Incumbent Councilman Harold Dietz left his debate podium empty on WHRC TV-15, and the internal tracking poll (44.6% to 44.2%) that triggered his fatal WTGA 790 AM radio attack on Katie's wheelchair ramp.
  8. Feb 4, 2016 — Majority Leader Callaway's Closed-Door Post-Mortem on HB 663 & The Pre-Floor Review That Never Happened
    What happened inside House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway's (R-Danville) Capitol office thirty minutes after HB 663 imploded on the floor—and the step-by-step pre-floor bill review in Room 518 with Katie and the thirteen-year-old Hawkins triplets (Sarah, Mandy, and Sam) that would have spared Delegate Martin Cobb his televised humiliation.
  9. Feb 5–6, 2016 — Why the House Page Triplets Bolted From Room 518 & How Uncle Richard Rescued Them
    Reveals how Uncle Richard Callaway and Aunt Marge rescued thirteen-year-old autistic triplets Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins in early 2015, why the triplets bolted from the doorway of Room 518 during Katie and Nate's Friday morning meltdown to fetch both Floor Leaders, and how Saturday Night Sketch (Studio 6B) wrote the viral HB 663 cold open without "cripping up."
  10. Jun 2026 – Jan 2027 — The $14 Million DSCC Primary Shock, Thorne's 'Broken Katie' Meltdown, & The Senate Wheelchair Caucus
    Inside retiring Senator Martin Warren's office and the DSCC when Katie and Nate's bus-riding campaign defeated Preston Holloway, Uncle Richard going live on Beacon News from Danville to defend Katie against President Garrett Thorne, the Architect of the Capitol's desk upgrades for the three-member U.S. Senate Wheelchair Caucus (Senator Tess Dunmore [D-IL], Senator Katie Prairie [D-VA], and Senator Josh Novak [D-IA]), and Vice President Conrad Drayton's fury in S-216 over swearing Katie in on the U.S. Constitution.
  11. Feb 16, 2027 — Inside Dirksen Room 511: Commissioner Sterling & Director Cross's Panic
    Follow the nine stages of bureaucratic collapse inside Dirksen Room 511 as DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and RRC Director Evelyn Cross wonder how a United States Senator knows the exact color of 2007 Level 2 Barton Hall passes, the MedStrip wound-closure strips on a girl's broken nose, and the lumpy bags of curtains inside a Rec Hall storage closet—until the math clicks (41 - 20 = 21) and Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence reads them the Riot Act from Richmond.
  12. Mar 2027 – Spring 2044 — Brenda Walsh's Suite 756 Cease-and-Desist, Thorne's Gag Order, & The 2044 Route 15 Bus-Stop Primary
    The complete story behind Brenda Walsh's unauthorized Tidewater Thorne & RTR Superstore in Suite 756 at Timberline Shopping Center (shut down by a Cease-and-Desist letter from Thorne Enterprises nine days after her own daughter voted to convict and bar Garrett Thorne for life), how a federal bail gag order (18 U.S.C. § 3142) silenced Thorne, and why fifty-eight-year-old three-term Senator Katie Prairie refused the 2044 Presidential Nomination at the CVTA Route #15 bus stop and forced every White House contender to interview on a live Virginia Beach city bus ("Wait!? A BUS!? HUH!?").
